intro: Looking for education consultants near you usually means you want someone local who understands the schools and admissions in your area. Perhaps you're choosing a school, preparing an application, or working through special educational needs or university choices. We can introduce you to a suitable UK education consultant who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for education consultants nearby usually need
need_lead: Most people get in touch because a decision about a child's education feels important and they want someone with experience to help them think it through.
needs: You are choosing between local schools and want help understanding admissions criteria and how to compare them.
You are preparing an application for a selective school or a particular year group and want help with the paperwork and deadlines.
Your child may have special educational needs and you want guidance on what support to ask for and how to put your case.
You are thinking about university choices and want help with course options, applications and personal statements.
You are considering an appeal after a school place decision and want help preparing your case for the panel.
context: Education consultancy is not regulated by a single body, so it is worth looking for a consultant with relevant teaching, admissions or special educational needs experience. Membership of organisations such as the Society of Education Consultants is one sign to look for, along with references and a clear written agreement setting out what they will do.

If your situation involves a school admission appeal, independent appeal panels in England follow the School Admission Appeals Code. A consultant can help you prepare, but the decision rests with the panel, so treat any firm promise of a particular outcome with caution.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Tell us the age of the child and the year group or stage they are at now.
Explain what you need help with, such as choosing a school, an application, special educational needs or university choices.
Mention the area you live in and any schools or institutions you are already considering.
Tell us about any deadlines you are working towards, such as an application closing date.
Share anything relevant about your child's needs, strengths or previous school experience.
Let us know whether you have already spoken to the school or local authority and what they said.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the education consultant
questions: What experience do you have with the schools and admissions in my area?
Have you worked with families in a similar situation to ours before?
What will you do for us, and how will you keep us informed?
What are your fees and how are they charged?
What deadlines should we be aware of for our application or appeal?
Will you put our agreement in writing before we start?

faqs.q: Can an education consultant help with a school admission appeal?
faqs.a: Yes, a consultant can help you prepare your case and understand the process. Independent appeal panels in England follow the School Admission Appeals Code, but the decision rests with the panel.

faqs.q: Do I need a consultant who is local to me?
faqs.a: Local knowledge of schools and admissions can be valuable, which is why many people search near them. It is still worth asking about their experience with the specific schools you are considering.

faqs.q: What should I look for in an education consultant?
faqs.a: Look for relevant teaching, admissions or special educational needs experience, and consider membership of organisations such as the Society of Education Consultants. Ask for references and a clear written agreement.

faqs.q: How much does an education consultant cost?
faqs.a: Fees vary depending on what you need, so quotes are on application. Ask the consultant to set out their fees clearly in writing before you agree to anything.
